prompt: Merge a pile of unsorted, overlapping {start, end} intervals into the smallest sorted set that covers the same ground, then report the total length covered. Complete merge and totalCovered in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Sorting by start turns the problem into a single sweep: keep a current interval and, for each following row, either extend its end (when the next start is at or before the current end) or close it off and begin a new one. The end must be extended with Math.max, since a later interval can be entirely inside the current one. Because the caller's array must not be disturbed, the rows are copied into a fresh array before sorting, and the merged rows are freshly allocated too.
hints: Sort first. Arrays.sort(copy, (a, b) -> Integer.compare(a[0], b[0])) puts the rows in start order so overlaps can only involve neighbours.
Sweep with two variables, start and end. The next row merges when nextStart <= end; when it does, end = Math.max(end, nextEnd) -- plain assignment loses a contained interval.
Do not forget to add the interval you are currently holding after the loop ends, and copy the rows before sorting so the caller's array keeps its original order.
